items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: But Beethoven, Bach and Brahms, they’re just as big as they ever were you know.

ctx.x: Yeah every couple of years you see it in the jazz magazines and I think it’s just like okay it’s time to write about that again, because it’s just something to write about.

Right. Because in the 70s the fusion started, they were saying jazz is dead. But then here comes Wynton Marsalis you know, playing more jazz than anybody ever played you know, and all these young people and jazz programs in colleges and universities. You know that’s the thing about America and a free society. It’s free speech you know, and people can say what they want to say, can believe what they want to be and you can’t get bent out of shape. You know if jazz is dead then classical music has got to be dead a…
Do you think that jazz education sort of the explosion of it in the last twenty years has been a good thing for the music?
